newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch estimate 1996 deficit at 2.2 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Dutch estimate 1996 deficit at 2.2 pct of GDP.

text.p: The 1996 Dutch public sector defict is provisionally estimated at 2.2 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said in a letter to parliament on Friday.

The figure is comfortably below the level of three percent of GDP needed to qualify for European economic and monetary union, though Zalm and his ministry had previously mentioned slightly lower figures for 1996.
Zalm said Dutch public sector debt was now provisionally estimated at 78.5 percent of GDP, well above the 60 percent formally required to qualify for EMU.
In its 1997 budget, presented to parliament last September, the government had estimated the 1996 deficit at 2.6 percent of GDP and the debt at 78.8 percent.
Zalm said central government spending for 1996 had turned out 1.2 billion guilders lower than estimated in the budget, while tax revenues had come in 4.7 billion guilders higher.
The 1997 budget had estimated the 1997 deficit at 2.2 percent of GDP and the debt at 76.2 percent of GDP.
Zalm said 1997 tax revenues were now expected to be some 2.7 billion guilders higher than estimated in the budget.
He is expected to send a progress report on the 1997 budget to parliament in April or May.
